results.matched_title: Missing authorization for updating a movie
Missing ownership check for movie update operation

baseline_findings.title: Missing ownership enforcement for movie update operation
baseline_findings.description: The `/api/movies/:movieId` route allows any authenticated user to update a movie, even if it does not belong to them. This could lead to unauthorized modifications of other users' movies.
baseline_findings.context_reasoning: The `checkAuth` middleware ensures that the user is logged in, but there is no check to ensure that the authenticated user is the owner of the movie being updated. The route handler directly updates the movie without verifying ownership.
baseline_findings.suggested_fix: Add an ownership check before updating the movie. For example: if (updateMovie.owner !== req.user._id) return res.status(403).json({ message: 'You are not authorized to update this movie' });

baseline_findings.title: Missing ownership check for movie update operation
baseline_findings.description: The `PATCH /api/movies/:movieId` endpoint allows any authenticated user to update a movie, regardless of whether they own the movie. This could lead to unauthorized modifications of other users' movies.
baseline_findings.context_reasoning: The `checkAuth` middleware ensures that only authenticated users can access this endpoint, but it does not check if the user is the owner of the movie being updated. The absence of an ownership check means any authenticated user can update any movie.
baseline_findings.suggested_fix: Add an ownership check to ensure the user updating the movie is the owner of the movie. This can be done by comparing `req.user._id` with `updateMovie.owner`. If they do not match, return a 403 Forbidden response.
